name: Outlook and Microsoft To Do Skills
description: Use the Microsoft Graph connector tools instead of automating Outlook or To Do.
instructions:
Never automate the Outlook or Microsoft To Do UI. When the Microsoft connector is set up (Settings → Connectors), these tools talk to the account directly:

Mail — the ordinary email tools cover Outlook, no separate tools exist:
1. list_emails returns rows whose ids start with 'ms:' when Outlook is the active backend.
2. read_email and mark_email_read route by that id prefix, so ids stay valid.
3. send_email always shows the user a confirmation dialog before anything leaves the device.
Note the backend order: if a Gmail connector is also set up, Gmail is used for new listings and sends. Existing 'ms:' ids still resolve to Outlook.

Tasks — list_tasks, create_task and complete_task read and write the user's real Microsoft To Do lists, which sync to their other devices. These are NOT the same as todowrite: todowrite is your own scratch plan for the current conversation and disappears afterwards. If the user says 'remind me to…', 'add to my to-do list', or 'put it on my list', they mean create_task. Use todowrite only to track your own steps through a multi-part request.

Calendar — use list_calendar_events / create_calendar_event with source='microsoft', and check_availability for free/busy questions.

If a tool reports that the sign-in expired or needs reconnecting, tell the user to reconnect in Settings → Connectors; do not try to work around it through the UI.
